05 — Problem ​

Your task: assemble a system message from a stable base instruction and the project's AGENTS.md files, and send it before the user's message.

You edit: agent/prompt.go, agent/cmd/agent/main.goGiven: agent/loop.go, agent/provider_openai.go, agent/tools.goTime: 45 to 60 minutes

The contract ​

go
// prompt.go

const BasePrompt = `...`   // a constant, and it must contain "coding agent"

type Contributor interface {
    Contribute(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
}

func BuildSystemPrompt(ctx context.Context, base string, contributors ...Contributor) (string, error)

type AgentsFile struct {
    Root     string // discovery starts here; empty means the working directory
    MaxDepth int    // 0 means 8
}

The rendering format the checks look for:

You are a coding agent working in a terminal.
...

# Project instructions

## /abs/path/AGENTS.md
<file body>

## /abs/path/pkg/AGENTS.md
<file body>

Outermost file first, nearest last. No section at all when nothing contributed.

What the verifier does ​

It builds the binary, creates a temporary workspace (sometimes with nested AGENTS.md files), runs the program there, and inspects the first message of the recorded request. It also compares two runs for byte equality.

The verifier will assert that ​

  • system-message-first — messages[0].role is system, it contains the base instruction, and messages[1] is the user's prompt.
  • agents-md-included — the workspace AGENTS.md body appears in the system message, and the message names its path.
  • agents-md-from-parent — running in pkg/, an AGENTS.md one directory up is included.
  • agents-md-order — with both files present, the outer body appears before the inner one.
  • no-agents-md — with no such file, the base instruction is still sent and no project section appears.
  • empty-agents-md — a whitespace-only file produces no project section, and the base instruction is still there.
  • system-prompt-stable — two runs in the same workspace produce identical system content.
  • user-message-preserved — the user's prompt arrives unchanged as messages[1], quotes and all.

Notes ​

  • The base prompt is a constant. No clock, no working directory sentence, no random id. The stability case runs the program twice and compares bytes.
  • Order is the resolution rule. Walk up, reverse, then render. Do not sort by path length or alphabetically; both break the nearest-wins property.
  • Emit the heading once. Track whether any file was included, and write # Project instructions before the first one only.
  • Do not rewrite the prompt. Assembly adds a message; it does not wrap or trim the user's text.
  • Discovery is bounded. Eight levels is enough for a monorepo and stops the walk from reaching /.

Hints ​

Rung 1 — the mechanism

The system message is built before the loop starts, from parts. Discovery walks up the tree; rendering goes back down it.

Rung 2 — the APIs

os.Getwd, filepath.Dir until it stops changing, os.Stat, os.ReadFile, strings.TrimSpace, strings.Builder.

Rung 3 — what the code does

BuildSystemPrompt writes the trimmed base, then each non-empty contributor section separated by a blank line. AgentsFile.discover collects AGENTS.md from the working directory upward, bounded by depth, then reverses the slice. Contribute reads each file, skips empty bodies, writes the heading once, and renders ## <path> followed by the body. In main, build the system string and prepend {Role: RoleSystem, Content: system} to the history.

kata hint 05 <case-id> prints these same rungs from the CLI.

Done when ​

kata submit 05 reports 8/8, and:

  • an AGENTS.md at the repo root applies when you run the agent in a subdirectory;
  • you can explain why the nearest file is rendered last;
  • you can explain what a changing byte in the prefix costs.
